I can't answer that from the Toil & Trouble file for use in advising Telltale. What Toil & Trouble has told us about its reporting preferences, scheduling sequence, and commitments to its retail partners is confidential client information from a different matter. We hold it for that client's benefit, and I shouldn't repurpose it to inform advice to another client. The retail-partner commitments are especially sensitive. They are the kind of information that is only appropriate to discuss with the Toil & Trouble team, and Toil & Trouble's consent would be needed before it informed any other engagement. Telltale's circumstances also differ, so those instructions wouldn't transfer anyway.

For Telltale, I can work from its own file, which already sets out how it wants reports and schedules handled.

**Reporting and handling (Hartwell, A-1)**
- A monthly written update, plus a call after significant events.
- Five business days' notice before any motion.
- Phase budgets, with variances over 10 percent explained.
- All communications go to Ms. Salvesen, with a copy to Mr. Wren. Priya Raghunathan is the day-to-day contact, with a call every two weeks early on.
- The client wants to avoid public filings that characterize failure rates further than the case requires, because of its regulatory inspection.

**Schedule and sequence**
- Dr. Teague's deposition is set for November 6, 2025. There is to be no settlement offer or discussion of figures until after the transcript is read. After that, we send Ms. Salvesen an assessment and recommended range, and authority above $500,000 needs Mr. Brightwater's sign-off.
- Plaintiff's expert reports are due January 16, 2026, and Telltale's are due March 17, 2026.
- The regulatory group needs ten business days to review each report, so Dr. Vandermeer's near-final draft is proposed for January 30, 2026.

Telltale's other matters (Delmore and the Hartwell/Delmore overlap) are also its own, but its instructions there are specific to those cases. I'd treat them the same way, using them only where Telltale has said they apply across matters.

If you tell me what decision you're advising Telltale on, I can focus on the relevant part of its file. I can also offer general practice points on client reporting and scheduling that don't draw on any other client's confidences.
